extracted.intended_audience: Habitat for Humanity communications, marketing, design, and affiliate staff (photographers, designers, copywriters, fundraisers)
extracted.subtask_description: Brand and creative standards for producing Habitat for Humanity communications (annual reports, marketing, photography, logos, color, typography and digital assets). Guidance is aimed at ensuring consistent, on-brand materials across affiliates and channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lasting, meaningful outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize strength, stability and shelter in headlines and opening paragraphs as lasting, meaningful outcomes of Habitat's work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use copy and quotes (e.g., CEO quote) to highlight specific lasting and meaningful outcomes such as better health, education and employment opportunities. Place this emphasis early (headline/opening paragraph) so it frames the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitive, specific role for aggregate numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate channels (e.g., annual report) to share and celebrate large aggregate numbers rather than everyday communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you must present large numbers, accompany them immediately with a photo and caption that put a human face on the work so the number doesn't stand alone. Consider audience ordering in charts (e.g., place U.S. data first for U.S.-based audiences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct request for support and web links
rubrics_metrics.description: Include links to the online annual report and website, and drive readers to habitat.org for family stories and donation asks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use boilerplate and calls to action that point audiences to the website for more information and to donate or volunteer. Make donation/volunteer asks clear in contexts such as annual reports and marketing messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative approach: brand attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: All creative pieces should visually express the brand and messaging: optimism, dynamism, authenticity and simplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a clean, streamlined, edited, and clutter-free look so communications are as clear as the brand vision. Imagery, color, type selection and layout should reinforce these attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography: put people first in context of shelter
rubrics_metrics.description: Images should reflect the brand by putting people first and placing them within the context of shelter and construction whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistently represent diversity in a natural and appropriate way; ensure imagery feels spontaneous, authentic, and uplifting/optimistic rather than staged. Prefer moments that evoke emotion over technically perfect but sterile photos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depicting need with dignity
rubrics_metrics.description: When showing need or hardship, subjects must be presented with dignity and not exploited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sensationalizing or demeaning depictions; imagine how you would want your own family portrayed. Use images that are respectful and that align with brand tenets of strength, stability and self-reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select emotional, real moments
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose photos or video clips that capture the 'moment' — real, emotional, evocative scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select images for the emotional reaction they produce rather than for perfect technical attributes. Images need not be technically perfect to move an audience. Check the Digital Asset Network before shooting locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homeowner photography: do and don't
rubrics_metrics.description: Homeowner photography should feel friendly, approachable, spontaneous and diverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly staged, emotionless images and photos that lack the element of home. Ensure subjects and settings communicate warmth and the sense of a lived-in home.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer photography: do and don't
rubrics_metrics.description: Volunteer photography should be inspiring, authentic, expressive, diverse and focused on individuals and small groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly staged, generic images that lack humanity. Avoid wide-angle shots showing entire build sites when the intent is to highlight volunteer impact and human expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need photography: do and don't
rubrics_metrics.description: Need photography should be dignified, human, realistic, respectful and reflect both local and global contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use images that feel overly staged, hopeless, gloomy or moody. Maintain respect and hope in compositions even when depicting hardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: House and material photography: do and don't
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs of houses and materials should be simple and artful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid gritty or overly complex imagery when the subject is housing elements or materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo background and focus rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Be attentive to backgrounds; keep backgrounds simple or out of focus so they don't distract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If background is cluttered or draws attention away, find another angle. For group photos, focus on the person nearest the camera; slight background blur for back rows is acceptable and looks natural.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo lighting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure good light on subjects' faces and avoid harsh mid-day sun or heavy shadows from hats/helmets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, shoot with sun at your back; early morning and late afternoon light are preferable. Check for harsh shadows caused by hard hats or caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment and resolution guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use equipment appropriate to the intended use: smart phone photos are generally sufficient for social media; high-resolution images required for print or prominent web placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 10-megapixel DSLR will produce better images than a 10-megapixel compact camera, which will be better than a 10-megapixel smartphone. Choose resolution based on final use and medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety and construction policy compliance in photos
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographed build site activity must meet Habitat's construction safety policies and standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be safe and ensure images capture correct safety procedures. Refer to the construction safety manual at my.habitat.org/constructionsafety/policiesstandards before publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo selection and editing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Let image quality determine use; reserve large-format positions for the very best images and limit digital alteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lower-quality images as thumbnails or insets. Severely limit software alterations: cropping and background lightening/shadowing to aid legibility are acceptable, but avoid excessive visual elements or color washes; black & white printing is acceptable when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo age and reuse timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use photographs of people older than three years in communications; check the status of individuals for photos older than one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photos without people (houses/materials) may be used past three years. Older photos may be used to illustrate history only if captions or accompanying text clearly indicate historical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captions as storytelling opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Use captions to extend the story beyond who/where/what and draw out important brand messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever space allows, craft captions that show transformation or outcomes (e.g., BEFORE/AFTER phrasing) and connect the photo to the larger Habitat message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary color palette and reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the specified primary color palette (bright blue, bright green, white, gray, black) to create a vibrant, friendly and optimistic brand look.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Pantone/CMYK/RGB/HEX values in the guide and consult actual PANTONE® coated color chips to accurately match colors. Use CMYK as a starting point and work with printers/designers to determine correct formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color usage restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not apply bright blue and bright green to the Habitat logo or Habitat ReStore identifier; brand colors should not be tinted (100% saturation maintained).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: black may be tinted in limited instances. For print: use 15% black for a light gray and 85% black for a dark gray. Do not alter the master color patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary and tertiary color usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the secondary palette for additional color needs (charts, infographics, accents); use the tertiary yellow sparingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrict yellow to pie charts, bar graphs and occasional accents; yellow should represent the least amount of color on any page and be carefully considered relative to bright green to avoid discord.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography: typeface choices and intended uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Neue Haas Grotesk (or Arial) as the sans-serif brand typeface and Minion Pro (or Palatino) as the serif for body copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neue Haas Grotesk is optimized for print and digital and is intended for callout/display text, headlines, subheads, small amounts of text and legal disclosures. Minion Pro is intended for larger amounts of body copy and long-form documents (grant proposals, annual reports). Enticing Script may be used only in small amounts for fundraising mailings; never use it in other contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography application: callout and display rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Set callout/display text flush left in Neue Haas Grotesk Display Medium, in lowercase (initial caps allowed for proper names), with tight letter-spacing and leading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Display Medium for large headlines and Text Regular for small headlines/subheads/legal. Apply proper kerning and monitor leading so ascenders/descenders do not overlap. Examples of incorrect kerning/leading are provided; avoid those mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography application: color and image overlay
rubrics_metrics.description: Callout/display text can be set in a primary color (bright blue recommended) on white or reversed to white out of a primary color or photographic image; transparent type over a photo is acceptable with conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the image is brand-appropriate and the type is positioned where it doesn't interfere with important image details. Maintain legibility when using transparent effects or reversed type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Icon usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use icons and accent illustrations sparingly and primarily in editorial contexts (infographics, story packages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Icons should be simple, clear and consistent; avoid elaborate, complex, highly detailed or overly abstract icons. Always use brand color palette for icons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo importance and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the Habitat logo as a primary identity asset; keep it easily seen, separate and clean in presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate use of the marks is both a responsibility and a requirement for Habitat-branded organizations. Read logo rules carefully to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global logo elements and ® requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The global logo consists of the symbol, wordmark, and registered trademark symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The registered trademark symbol (®) provides notice of trademark rights and must never be removed from the mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo format preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the horizontal logo format as the primary preferred presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate formats (vertical, single-line) are allowed only when the preferred horizontal format will not work effectively due to space constraints and should be used only as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended logo restrictions (DO NOTs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extended logos may be used by Habitat-branded entities but must not be altered in various ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT add elements to the logo; modify or separate the people graphic; screen or tint the logo; outline the logo; use the logo as a watermark/background; place the logo on a busy pattern; add drop shadows or effects; change proportions; use non-master colors or change color pattern; use the logo in grayscale (unless explicitly allowed); add a tagline to the logo; use previous versions of the logo; or use other identifiers in place of the current logo. Maintain arrangement order and proportions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended logo signature line and translation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Extended logos may include upper and/or lower signature lines for local Habitat entity names but must follow format rules and translation approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature lines must follow legally registered names but may omit words such as Inc., of, the, in, for. Canada-specific rules: upper signature is not used; Quebec affiliates must use French-dominant or French translations. Translated logos require approval from Habitat for Humanity International Marketing, Branding and Publications in coordination with area communications staff. The global logo (without entity name) is reserved for Habitat for Humanity International and must not be used by affiliates without express permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo color usage (black-and-white guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Logo color choices should follow the guide; black-and-white treatments are outlined for compatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because brand elements are bright, express the logo primarily in one color for clarity and compatibility. Follow the guide's further specifics about allowed monochrome treatments and where to apply them.
